chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said to Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān:
O Yūnus, do not swear by disassociating from us, for whoever swears by disassociating from us, whether truthful or lying, has indeed dissociated from us.

key_terms.اَلصَّادِقُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the speaker of the hadith
key_terms.بَرِئَ: became dissociated or absolved from; indicating the serious consequence stated in the hadith
key_terms.بِالْبَرَاءَةِ: by dissociation or disavowal; the formula being prohibited in the oath
key_terms.صَادِقًا: truthfully; even if the speaker is telling the truth
key_terms.كَاذِبًا: falsely; even if the speaker is lying
key_terms.لَا تَحْلِفْ: do not swear; a prohibition against making such an oath
key_terms.مِنَّا: from us, referring to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام forbid swearing by dissociation from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام forbids invoking dissociation from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام as a form of oath. The hadith stresses the gravity of such wording, declaring that one who swears by it—whether truthfully or falsely—has in fact disassociated himself from them.
